subject: physics
question_text: Discuss the isochoric process and the isobaric process.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Short Answer Question 11 (printed p.130). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: isochoric has ΔV = 0 so W = 0 and ΔQ = ΔU = nC_VΔT; isobaric has W = PΔV = nRΔT and, by the first law with Mayer's relation C_P = C_V + R, ΔQ = nC_PΔT; the isochoric line is vertical and the isobaric line horizontal on a P–V diagram. C_V and C_P here are MOLAR specific heats.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The isochoric process
lines: An isochoric process holds volume
fixed, so no work is done:
On a P–V diagram it is a vertical
line. Example: a gas heated inside
a rigid, closed vessel.
steps.margin_note: First mark. W = 0, the vertical P–V line, and the rigid-vessel example.
steps.why: Work is P dV, and dV = 0 throughout a fixed-volume process, so the work is zero however the pressure changes.
common_mistakes: Confusing this with the isobaric line, which is horizontal, not vertical.
Saying no work is done because pressure is constant — pressure is NOT constant here, volume is.

recall.must_convey: That an isochoric process has W equal to zero, is a vertical line on a P V diagram, with the example of a gas heated in a rigid closed vessel.

steps.memory_tip: Isochoric: fixed VOLUME, vertical line, zero work — nothing to push against.

steps.label: Isochoric heat
lines: With W = 0, the first law
ΔQ = ΔU + W gives
All the heat supplied raises the
internal energy; none of it is
spent doing work.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. ΔQ = ΔU = n C_V ΔT, from the first law with W = 0.
steps.why: With no work to share the heat with, every joule supplied goes straight into raising the internal energy — that is why C_V, the constant-volume specific heat, appears here.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔQ = n C_P ΔT — C_P belongs to the isobaric process, not this one.
Forgetting to set W = 0 before applying the first law.

recall.must_convey: That delta Q equals delta U equals n C V delta T for the isochoric process.

steps.memory_tip: No work to share the heat with: ALL of it raises the internal energy.

steps.label: The isobaric process
lines: An isobaric process holds
pressure fixed, so the work done
is
On a P–V diagram it is a
horizontal line. Example: water
heated in an open vessel at
atmospheric pressure.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. W = P ΔV = nR ΔT, the horizontal line, and the open-vessel example.
steps.why: Pressure is fixed here, so the work is simply pressure times the change in volume, and PΔV can be rewritten as nRΔT using the gas equation.
common_mistakes: Confusing this with the isochoric line, which is vertical, not horizontal.
Writing W = V ΔP instead of W = P ΔV — pressure is what stays fixed.

recall.must_convey: That an isobaric process has W equal to P delta V equal to n R delta T, is a horizontal line, with the example of water heated in an open vessel.

steps.memory_tip: Isobaric: fixed PRESSURE, horizontal line, work is P times ΔV.

steps.label: Isobaric heat
lines: By the first law, ΔQ = ΔU + W =
n C_V ΔT + nR ΔT. Using Mayer's
relation C_P = C_V + R, this is
More heat is needed than at
constant volume, because part of
it now also does work.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. ΔQ = n C_P ΔT, reached through Mayer's relation.
steps.why: At constant pressure the heat has two jobs — raising the internal energy AND doing work — so it needs the larger specific heat C_P, which is exactly C_V + R more per mole.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔQ = n C_V ΔT here — that is the isochoric relation, not this one.
Forgetting Mayer's relation and leaving the answer as n C_V ΔT + nR ΔT unsimplified.

recall.must_convey: That delta Q equals n C P delta T for the isobaric process, reached through Mayer's relation C P equals C V plus R.
accept: delta Q equals n C P delta T
C P equals C V plus R
reject: delta Q equals n C V delta T

steps.memory_tip: Constant pressure needs C_P, the LARGER specific heat — heat here also has to do work.

insider_note: The heat relations are where marks are lost — an answer that states W = 0 and W = PΔV but never reaches ΔQ = nC_VΔT and ΔQ = nC_PΔT has written only half of this answer.
